Here's what I found on running LFM2.5-2.6B in the browser via ONNX/Transformers.js/WebGPU:

## The modelLFM2.5-2.6B is part of LFM2.5, a family of hybrid models designed for on-device deployment, building on the LFM2 architecture with a 128K context window and agentic post-training. It's a 2.69B-parameter model with 30 layers (22 double-gated short convolution blocks and 8 GQA layers), a 128K vocabulary, and a 131,072-token context window. It ships with day-one support across the inference ecosystem, including llama.cpp, MLX, vLLM, SGLang, and ONNX.

Liquid AI's own launch post points at a browser demo directly: "Try: run the WebGPU demo in your browser, no setup needed." A WebGPU space on Hugging Face runs a research agent fully in the browser.

## Official ONNX pathLiquid recommends ONNX for cross-platform deployment, edge devices, and browser-based inference with WebGPU and Transformers.js — ONNX models run on CPUs, GPUs, NPUs, and in browsers via WebGPU. LiquidONNX is the official tool for exporting LFM models to ONNX and running inference, available at `github.com/Liquid4All/onnx-export`, with a `lfm2-export` command that takes a model ID and a `--precision` flag (fp16, q4, q8). That's the route for producing a 2.6B ONNX build if a prebuilt one isn't already published.

The Transformers.js usage pattern from [Liquid's ONNX docs](https://docs.liquid.ai/deployment/on-device/onnx) is:

```js
import { AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoTokenizer, TextStreamer } from "@huggingface/transformers";
const model = await AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(modelId, {
  device: "webgpu",
  dtype: "q4", // or "fp16"
});
```

## Existing ONNX repos & demos
- [`onnx-community/LFM2-2.6B-ONNX`](https://huggingface.co/onnx-community/LFM2-2.6B-ONNX) — the previous-gen 2.6B ONNX export (uploaded by Xenova in response to a transformers.js request on the model repo). Useful as a reference for the 2.6B-scale ONNX shape/config.
- [`LiquidAI/LFM2-2.6B-Transcript-ONNX`](https://huggingface.co/LiquidAI/LFM2-2.6B-Transcript-ONNX) — an official LiquidAI 2.6B ONNX repo tagged `onnxruntime` and `webgpu`.
- [lfm2.5-thinking-web](https://github.com/sitammeur/lfm2.5-thinking-web) — a web app demonstrating LFM2.5-1.2B-Thinking in the browser using Transformers.js and ONNX Runtime Web, with real-time streaming responses running locally via WebGPU. It runs the model in a Web Worker (`worker.js`) — a good architectural template.
- [lfm-2.5-230m.lab](https://github.com/kortexa-ai/lfm-2.5-230m.lab) — loads `LiquidAI/LFM2.5-230M-ONNX` with `device: "webgpu"`, with selectable quantization that caches separately: q4 (~200 MB) is the default and best on phones. Inference runs in a Web Worker so the UI stays responsive; tokens stream via TextStreamer.

## Notes relevant to your loader code
- **Precision/shader-f16:** Bigger variants use proportionally more GPU memory and decode slower (memory-bandwidth-bound) — q4 is the right pick for memory-constrained devices. Since the LFM2.5 ONNX exports offer q4 alongside fp16, your `needsShaderF16(spec)` check can likely be relaxed for a q4 LFM2.5 spec — that gives you a genuine fallback to name in `classifyLocalModelError` instead of the generic "try a smaller browser model."
- **Memory budget:** The model runs in under 2.5 GB of memory, which is a plausible WebGPU buffer target but well above your Gemma-class defaults — worth gating on adapter limits.
- **Chat template / tool calls:** LFM2-family templates are text-only ChatML-like, so they take a plain string rather than typed content parts — matching the `spec.kind === "multimodal"` branch you're editing. Function definitions go in as JSON objects between `<|tool_list_start|>`/`<|tool_list_end|>` tokens in the system prompt, and the model writes Pythonic function calls between `<|tool_call_start|>` and `<|tool_call_end|>`, with results returned between `<|tool_response_start|>` and `<|tool_response_end|>` as a "tool" role. Note LFM2.5 additionally emits a `<think>` block before answering, so your streaming parser needs to strip or surface that.

**Bottom line:** there is no confirmed `onnx-community/LFM2.5-2.6B-ONNX` repo in these results — the official ONNX 2.6B artifacts I can verify are LFM2 (not 2.5) or the Transcript variant. Check the Hugging Face ONNX community org directly, or export it yourself with `uv run lfm2-export LiquidAI/LFM2.5-2.6B --precision q4`.

content.text:
Built the eval harness. Here's what I found scoping it, then how to run it.

## Three things that change the shape of this

**1. The tool surface is one tool, not many.** `quote_passage` (`convex/agentTools.ts:106`) is the only tool in the codebase, wired into persona-feedback on both paths (`src/utils/ai-client.ts:982`, `convex/agents.ts:291`) with `stopWhen: stepCountIs(3)`. So "can it call all the tools" is a narrow bar. The wider risk is the ~7 strict-JSON tasks a 2.6B model also has to serve — rubric/evidence/integrity/target-fit judges, `research-extract` — where a malformed brace fails the feature outright.

**2. None of your five existing evals touch tools.** They all go through `evals/llm-client.ts` → Portkey `chat/completions` with a bare system+user body, no `tools` key. So the harness you have literally cannot answer this question — hence a new script rather than a flag on an old one.

**3. The one that would have bitten you.** `generateTrackedText` discards and re-runs any reply where `hasReasoningTags(text)` is true. LFM2.5's chat template *always* opens a `<think>` block, so **every call would silently cost two** — on the slowest engine in the product. The retry even nudges "do not place your whole answer inside `<think>` tags," which that model cannot comply with. Free mode needs a per-provider "reasoning expected" flag before this ships. The eval counts this as `wouldRegenerate` so you see it as a number rather than trusting my reading.

Also worth knowing: there's no AI SDK provider for transformers.js. LFM2.5 emits Pythonic calls between `<|tool_call_start|>`/`<|tool_call_end|>`, so someone has to write a `LanguageModelV2` adapter doing tool→system-prompt rendering plus token parsing. That adapter is most of the browser risk, and it's not the model's fault if it fails.

## What I built

`evals/run-local-model.ts` → `bun run eval:local`. It runs the **real** production path — your prompt builders, your actual `quote_passage` (wrapped, not reimplemented, so the schema and description under test are the shipping ones), `generateText` with the same `stepCountIs(3)`. Only the endpoint changes.

Two runs per case so the two competences separate: `tools` and a `notools` control. If analysis holds up without the tool and collapses with it, that's the tool, not the model's reading.

```bash
llama-server -hf LiquidAI/LFM2.5-2.6B-GGUF --jinja -c 8192
LOCAL_MODEL_BASE_URL=http://localhost:8080/v1 bun run eval:local
```

It writes `local-model-scores.json` (per-case metrics + aggregate) and `local-model-runs.json` in the exact shape `evals/judge.ts` reads — so `cp evals/local-model-runs.json evals/runs.json && bun run eval:judge` grades analysis quality on the same faithfulness/helpfulness rubrics as your hosted models. Small model judged on the incumbent's terms.

Headline metric is `anchoredRate` — not "did it call the tool" but "did the note end up pinned to a real passage," which is the thing that actually degrades. If tool calls come back zero with no errors, it warns you to check `--jinja` before blaming the model.

**Verified** against a mock emitting real tool calls: all five tool metrics reach 1, and the `<think>` detector fires. I deleted the mock output files so nobody mistakes them for real numbers.

## Recommended order

Run it on llama.cpp first. Browser is q4 — it can only be worse than the GGUF, so if the weights fail here the browser port is dead and you've spent an afternoon instead of a fortnight. If it passes, port and re-run the same harness to isolate the quantization delta.

# Treat reasoning models as first-class, and stream them

## Context

Scoping LFM2.5-2.6B as the signed-out / free-mode engine turned up a
structural assumption: the codebase treats reasoning output as a defect to be
recovered from, not a mode to be supported.

Three sites discard the whole generation and call again whenever the reply
contains a `<think>` block — not when the reply is unusable, merely when the
channel was touched. LFM2.5's chat template *always* opens `<think>`, so every
note would silently cost two calls on the slowest engine in the product. The
retry even instructs the model "do not place your whole answer inside `<think>`
tags," which that model cannot obey.

Streaming has the matching gap. The server persona path doesn't stream at all,
and the client streams only visible prose — so a model that thinks first shows
a blank panel for many seconds, because the persona card is filtered on
non-empty text.

The outcome we want: reasoning is an expected mode, never a reason to
regenerate; every persona note streams from both client and server; and the
reader sees the room start thinking immediately, with the option to watch it.

Most of the machinery already exists and is simply unwired — see Change 2.

## Change 1 — Reasoning is expected, not a defect

Three sites, same shape:
`src/utils/ai-client.ts:759`, `convex/agents.ts:309`, `convex/agents.ts:409`.

- Condition `if (!visible || hasReasoningTags(text))` becomes `if (!visible)`.
  Regenerate only when nothing visible survived stripping — a truncated or
  unclosed block — never merely because the model reasoned.
- Change the retry nudge to something obeyable: "Close your `<think>` block,
  then write the note." When the second attempt is also empty, keep the
  existing `removeReasoningTagMarkers` salvage.
- Rewrite the `hasReasoningTags` doc comment (`src/utils/reasoning-tags.ts:5-13`)
  — it currently documents the discard policy as the intent, and would
  otherwise re-teach the removed behaviour to the next reader.

Everything else that calls `stripReasoningTags` (llm-parsing, research-targets,
the judge paths) is already correct and needs no change.

## Change 2 — Use the accumulator that already exists

`src/utils/generation-stream.ts` already implements exactly what's needed:
native `reasoning-delta` parts *and* inline `<think>` tags, independent text
and reasoning lifecycles, and an `activePart` telling a view which is
receiving deltas. It has **zero imports and no test** — fully built, never
wired up. Press it into service rather than writing anything new.

Leave `src/utils/interview-stream.ts` alone. It layers DOSSIER/PROBE contract
masking over the same idea; folding the two together is a separate change.

## Change 3 — Client streaming becomes reasoning-aware

- `runOnce` (`src/utils/ai-client.ts:648-694`) consumes `result.fullStream`
  instead of `result.textStream`, feeding `createGenerationStreamAccumulator`.
  Native reasoning parts stop being invisible; `createVisibleTextFilter` is
  replaced by the accumulator.
- Widen `StreamText` (`src/utils/ai-client.ts:634`) from
  `(visibleSoFar: string) => void` to `(snapshot: GenerationStreamSnapshot) => void`.
- Update call sites that assign `store.streamingNotes[id] = partial` —
  `personas-panel.tsx` (three, near :678, :982, :1288), `comments-panel.tsx:385`,
  `background-room.ts:392` — to read `snapshot.text`, plus the new reasoning
  fields.
- `runAiWithFallback` (`src/utils/ai-orchestrator.ts:65`) gains an optional
  `onText` pass-through; today it drops streaming entirely for every feature
  routed through it.

## Change 4 — Server streaming for persona notes

Mirror the interview pattern, which already works end to end.

- `convex/schema.ts`: new `personaNoteStreams` table, same shape and indexes as
  `dossierInterviewStreams` (`convex/schema.ts:18-32`).
- `convex/personaNoteStreams.ts`: new, mirroring `convex/interviewStreams.ts` —
  `get` query, `write` internalMutation, `clear` mutation, same
  `authenticatedUserId` guard.
- `runLlm` (`convex/agents.ts:274-376`) takes an optional `streamId`. When
  present, use `streamText` + `fullStream` following the interview loop at
  `convex/agents.ts:803-828`, writing snapshots through the new mutation.
  Tools and `stopWhen: stepCountIs(3)` are unchanged — tool calls must keep
  working while streaming.
- Client subscribes to the stream and merges into the same store fields the
  client path writes, so the UI has one shape regardless of which path ran.

## Change 5 — Thinking UI

`personas-panel.tsx:2164-2201` currently filters streaming cards on non-empty
text, which is why a thinking model renders nothing.

- Render the card whenever the persona has an active stream — text, reasoning,
  or running status — so it appears the moment generation starts.
- Add a `▸ thinking` disclosure fed by `snapshot.reasoning`, driven by
  `activePart === "reasoning"`. Collapsed by default; collapses on its own once
  prose begins. Must survive the letterpress/typewriter styling.

## Tests

- `src/utils/reasoning-tags.test.ts` — existing cases encode the discard
  policy; update them to the new contract.
- `src/utils/generation-stream.test.ts` — new. Cover native reasoning parts,
  inline tags, tags split across chunk boundaries, and an unclosed block.
- `src/utils/ai-client.test.ts` — assert **no** second call when reasoning tags
  are present alongside visible text, and that a second call still happens when
  nothing visible survives.

Run these files individually — the full suite has pre-existing cross-file
interference unrelated to this change.

## Verification

1. `bun run build.types` and `bun test` on the three files above.
2. `bun run eval:local` against llama.cpp serving LFM2.5
   (`llama-server -hf LiquidAI/LFM2.5-2.6B-GGUF --jinja -c 8192`). Confirm
   `anchoredRate` holds and that no case issues two generations — the metric
   this whole change exists to fix.
3. Run the app against a reasoning model and watch a persona note: the card
   should appear immediately in a thinking state, the disclosure should hold
   the reasoning, and prose should stream in without the panel blanking.
